text:
maya: Heads-up — I'm starting a small migration proposal: collapse the per-route wide telemetry table into a compact events table + JSONB attributes, with a small set of derived materialized columns for the Console dashboards. want to discuss parity gating for quotas and dashboards

ashley: curious — what's the main pain we're solving? storage or query perf?

maya: both. the current wide table has 60 nullable route_* columns, lots of churn when we add metrics. storage doubled and dashboard queries scan tons of columns. also makes rollouts painful because schema changes block deploys.

tom: +1. also adding a column requires consumers to update SQL everywhere. compact events + attributes would avoid DDLs for new telemetry.

kevin: tradeoff is query speed. dashboards need fast aggregations for last-30d per-route QPS/latency. JSONB can be slow if we rely on ->> filtering. what's the plan for indexes/derived cols?

maya: plan sketch: write schema: events(route_id text, ts timestamptz, metric_name text, value double precision, attrs jsonb). then materialize common metrics into a tiny route_metrics_latest table populated by background job / stream processor (route_id, ts, qps, p95, error_rate). dashboards query the materialized table for realtime, fallback to pre-aggregate if missing.

jen: Sounds sensible. How do we handle parity gating so quotas (which are strict) don't break at cutoff?

maya: propose shadow-write period: dual-write to old wide_table and new events+materialized. run parity checker job that compares computed quota usage between systems every 10m, alert on >0.5% divergence. Only flip enforcement after 7 days of parity.

ashley: do we have capacity for dual-write load? replicated writes will increase IOPS. sizing callout needed.

tom: we can throttle parity job sampling to 1% of routes initially. also can run dual-write only for routes above threshold (active routes).

kevin: what about high-cardinality attrs? routes have tags and labels that explode cardinality. JSONB keeps them but we need TTL/compaction to avoid index growth.

maya: agree — attrs store raw tags but we'll enforce a sanitized attributes whitelist before write. long tail dropped into a cold store for ad-hoc debugging.

jen: dashboards: we should update Console queries to prefer materialized table and add transparency: a banner 'metrics are computed from materialized aggregates; raw events available for ad-hoc'. UX owners ok?

ashley: nice. rollout UX: feature flag per-organization so we can enable events-only for a small cohort first. also add a rollback path: replicate materialized->wide_table for 24h if we need to revert quickly.

tom: can we show a short SQL snippet for parity check?

maya: paste:
```sql
-- sample parity check for qps over 10m window
select route_id, abs(a.qps - b.qps)/greatest(a.qps,1) as rel_diff
from wide_qps a
join materialized_qps b using (route_id)
where a.ts = b.ts and a.ts > now() - interval '10 minutes'
order by rel_diff desc limit 50;
```

kevin: ok. alerting: trigger if >1 route has rel_diff > 0.02 in last hour or aggregated weighted diff >0.005.

jen: backfill plan for materialized table? full rebuild + incremental stream. backfill should run in batches and mark progress to avoid reprocessing.

maya: yes — steps: 1) start shadow dual-write, 2) run initial backfill job per-shard, 3) enable parity checker + alerts, 4) enroll small cohort behind flag, 5) 7-day parity window, 6) flip enforcement and retire wide table after another cooldown.

ashley: ops questions: who owns the backfill job and runbook? can we add a runbook entry in eng-platform?

maya: i'll draft the runbook. owners: tom (backfill infra), kevin (parity checker + alerts), jen (console query changes / UX banner), ashley (capacity sign-off).

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: feature-flag infra change will be deployed to staging at 2024-06-05T21:00Z if no blockers.

tom: action items for today: maya to post PR sketching tables + stream processor; kevin to prototype parity query + alert; jen to draft dashboard query changes; ashley to run quick capacity estimate.

maya: thanks all — i'll post the PR by EOD and link the runbook draft in #eng-platform. :thumbsup:
